name: arc-partitioned-marker-line-fill
description: Use when ARC grids have 8-colored separators and sparse 2/3 markers. Fill straight segments between aligned same-color markers.
---

# ARC partitioned marker line fill

Use this when an ARC input is divided into rectangular chambers by complete rows and columns of color 8, with sparse single-cell markers (notably colors 2 and 3) inside chambers.

## Procedure

1. Identify all full separator rows and columns of 8. Treat the open rectangular regions between separators as cells of a higher-level chamber grid; the chambers need not all have the same size (e.g. a narrower final chamber is possible).
2. Map every marker to its chamber coordinate and color, ignoring its precise within-chamber offset.
3. For each pair of same-color markers aligned in the same chamber row or same chamber column, fill the inclusive straight corridor between their chambers with that color. Do not extend beyond the endpoints. Multiple aligned pairs may form a longer line; process all markers/segments.
4. Leave unfilled chambers unchanged (typically 0), and preserve all separator 8s.
5. Where differently colored filled corridors intersect, use the observed overlap color. In the demonstrated 2/3 case, the intersection is 6.
6. Expand the chamber-level result back to the original grid dimensions by filling every pixel of each affected chamber uniformly; retain the 8 separator bands exactly.

## Verification

Before submitting, check that each colored chamber belongs to a segment connecting aligned same-color marker endpoints, that line intersections are handled consistently, that no segment extends outside its endpoints, and that chamber dimensions/separators are preserved.

## Demonstrated pattern

A 5x5 chamber grid with two 2 markers aligned vertically and two 3 markers aligned horizontally produced filled inclusive corridors; their crossing chamber became 6. A larger example included intersecting aligned pairs and a shorter final chamber, confirming that the rule is applied at chamber level rather than by raw pixel coordinates.",
